amendments.because: Narrowed under the owner's Harm 1-2 rule: a finding's title plus who is affected needs two sentences; one sentence would drop who is affected (Gain 1, Harm 1)

findings.body: Raise: Not done. Task stops copy the plan row's Name and What it delivers directly into the owner's question. The task row in plans/FORGE-DOCTORFIX-1.md:326, for example, describes delivery with command flags, output labels and internal tooling. If that task's review loop stops, the owner receives those implementation details instead of the promised plain-words account of what the item delivers. The named close proof uses a fix, so it does not exercise this task path.
findings.title: Not done: stopped task questions expose implementation text instead of a plain delivery

findings.body: Raise: Functional. This scan reports stopped specs from every worktree, but prints a bare `forge read <slug> --resolve ...` command. `forge next` can run from the main checkout, while `forge read` resolves a spec in the current checkout (`src/forge/story.py:901-905`). For a spec stopped on a story or fix branch and absent from main, following the printed next step refuses with `no_spec` instead of recording the owner's choice. The named read proof runs `forge next` from the spec's own worktree, so it misses this normal path.
findings.title: forge next gives an unusable resolve command for a stopped spec in another worktree

stop.reason: Owner rule for Harm 1-2: findings 2 and 3 are fixed in commit bc9156411 (land's stop ends with the resolve line; tests check delivery and all three choices); finding 1 (follow-up fixes named by the finding title) is Gain 2, lived with: those names come from the follow-up generator

why: When a cold read or review loop stops, the owner is asked to accept, narrow or split with no context; with many items in parallel they can't tell what the item is or what was flagged
